questions.text: Situation: A developer has an array of products: const products = [{ id: 1, name: 'Laptop', price: 45000, inStock: true }, { id: 2, name: 'Mouse', price: 1200, inStock: false }, { id: 3, name: 'Keyboard', price: 2500, inStock: true }]; They want to create a new array containing only the names of products that are in stock. Which code accomplishes this?
options: products.reduce((acc, p) => { if (p.inStock) acc.push(p.name); return acc; }, [])

questions.text: Situation: An Express app serves student data. The route GET /api/students/:id should return a single student object. However, the developer wrote: app.get('/api/students/:id', (req, res) => { const student = students.find(s => s.id === req.params.id); res.json(student); }); If no student matches the ID, what is the problem and how should it be fixed?
options: The code works fine; it returns null
The code crashes because find returns undefined; should check and return 404
The ID parameter is accessed incorrectly; should use req.body.id
The route path is wrong; should be /api/students?id=:id

questions.text: Situation: A developer is building a Docker image for a Node.js app. They use this Dockerfile: FROM node:20-alpine WORKDIR /app COPY . . RUN npm install CMD ["node", "server.js"] The build is slow because npm install runs every time, even when only source code changes. How should they optimize this?
options: Copy package*.json before COPY . and run npm install before copying the rest of the source
